papers.title: Authoritarian Persuasion at Home and Abroad: The Partial Effectiveness of Foreign Influencers in Propaganda Work
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · direct foreign-influencer evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Two preregistered survey experiments with 4,800 respondents in China and the United States tested soft-propaganda videos in which either an American or a Chinese influencer described freedom in China. Foreign influencers did not persuade Chinese audiences, but American respondents evaluated pro-China messages more favorably when the speaker was a fellow American. The study directly identifies co-national source identity as a boundary condition for foreign-influencer persuasion about China.

papers.title: Where the World Connects: How Intergroup Contact on Social Media Influences Intergroup Outcomes
papers.authors: Yansheng Liu, Yilan Guo, Alex Paloma, Mary Beth Oliver, et al.
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · adjacent intergroup-contact mechanism
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Two 2 × 3 online experiments with Chinese RedNote users (combined N = 833) varied whether a post came from an American or Chinese user and whether it appeared in English, Chinese, or both languages. Exposure to the American poster increased inclusion of Americans in the self, moral regard, and willingness to interact, with perceived connectedness operating as a mechanism. Although it does not study IShowSpeed, it offers a close causal model for how social-media contact with an out-group creator can change intergroup responses.

papers.title: Machine Translation in the Wild: User Reaction to Xiaohongshu’s Built-In Translation Feature
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 26th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation, 813–825
papers.category: X自动翻译 · direct platform-feature evidence · fallback tier
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: The study analyzes 6,723 comments from 11 official Xiaohongshu posts announcing the platform’s built-in machine-translation feature. Sentiment and thematic analyses show generally positive reactions alongside concerns about functionality, accessibility, and accuracy. Users often stress-tested the feature with slang, abbreviations, isolated expressions, and encoded forms rather than ordinary conversation, and successful decoding sometimes encouraged uncritical trust in translation output. The platform differs from X, but the feature launch and user-response setting closely match the proposed research problem.

papers.title: Analysing Mistranslation of Emotions in Multilingual Tweets by Online MT Tools
papers.authors: Hadeel Saadany, Constantin Orasan, Rocio Caro Quintana, Felix Do Carmo, and Leonardo Zilio
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 24th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation, 275–284
papers.category: X自动翻译 · direct Twitter evidence · fallback tier
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This study evaluates whether automatic translation preserves emotion in multilingual tweets. It finds cases in which mistranslation removes the original emotion or reverses its sentiment, identifies Twitter-specific linguistic features that create translation difficulty across language pairs, and shows that standard machine-translation quality metrics can give false confidence when emotion is distorted in short, telegraphic messages. The paper is directly tied to Twitter/X content but evaluates translation fidelity rather than downstream interaction behavior.

papers.title: Human Well-Being at Work with AI: Development and Validation of the AI Workplace Well-Being (AWWB) Scale
papers.authors: Mengshi Yang, Tanhao Gao, Jingnan Zhao, and Min Hua
papers.venue: International Journal of Human–Computer Interaction, OnlineFirst
papers.category: AI与幸福感 · direct workplace measurement
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: The article develops and validates the AI Workplace Well-Being Scale using 1,191 participants across three independent samples: exploratory factor analysis (n = 371), confirmatory factor analysis (n = 370), and external validation (n = 450). It is directly useful for distinguishing workplace AI well-being from generic job satisfaction or broad technology attitudes.

papers.title: Examining the Impact of Daily AI-Supported Work on Employee Outcomes: A Challenge-Hindrance Approach
papers.authors: Kanimozhi Narayanan, Claudia Sacramento, Wladislaw Rivkin, Mohsen Joshanloo, Matthew Carter, and Anitha Chinnaswamy
papers.category: AI与幸福感 · direct workplace process evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: A 10-day diary study of 173 U.S. employees models AI-supported work as both a challenge and a hindrance. On higher-AI-work days, challenge appraisal was associated with task crafting and innovative behavior, while hindrance appraisal triggered job-replacement anxiety and greater organizational cynicism. Favorable general evaluations of AI weakened the hindrance pathway. The findings show why the same workplace AI exposure can produce both beneficial and harmful employee outcomes.

papers.title: The cultural dissemination of web celebrity on safeguarding China’s intangible cultural heritage: a case study of Li Ziqi
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Using Stuart Hall’s encoding/decoding framework, this working paper examines seven Li Ziqi videos about Chinese intangible cultural heritage and associated audience comments. It argues that the videos encode heritage as an idealized Eastern lifestyle and aesthetic practice, while audience responses include dominant identification and negotiated readings such as cultural pride and knowledge supplementation. The paper is useful for reception categories, but its review status and sampling limits require caution.

papers.title: CULTURE-CMT: Benchmarking Contextualized Social Media Translation
papers.authors: Linjuan Wu, Dingming Li, Yiwen Qiu, Xinze Lyu, Ye Guo, Daoxin Zhang, Zhe Xu, and Weiming Lu
papers.category: Preprint · X自动翻译 · not peer reviewed
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This preprint introduces CULTURE-CMT, a Chinese–English benchmark of 572 manually verified social-media comment translations organized around slang, conversational context, and cases requiring both. Providing surrounding interaction context improves most model configurations but does not eliminate culturally ineffective translations; cases combining contextual dependence and culturally situated language remain especially difficult. The study is newer than other directly relevant arXiv candidates and helps specify when an automatic-translation feature may misrepresent platform conversation.

papers.title: Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI
papers.authors: Eleanor W. Dillon, Sonia Jaffe, Nicole Immorlica, and Christopher T. Stanton
papers.category: Preprint · AI与幸福感 · not peer reviewed
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: A field experiment across 66 firms and 7,137 knowledge workers randomly assigned access to a generative-AI tool embedded in email, meeting, and writing applications. Among treated workers who used the tool, weekly email time fell by roughly two hours and work outside regular hours decreased during the second half of the six-month study, while the overall quantity and composition of tasks did not measurably change. The results provide behavioral evidence on a work-life pathway rather than a direct happiness scale.

toc.abstractEn: Passive metering is used to measure how people combine multiple social platforms in everyday repertoires, addressing limitations of self-reports and single-platform behavioral data.

toc.abstractEn: An ethnographic content analysis documents how racially traumatic social-media content affects Black youths’ well-being and how platform systems participate in the circulation of that harm.

toc.abstractEn: The study adapts the discursive-opportunity framework to show how social bots alter visibility, resonance, and legitimacy in online protest discourse.

toc.title: Careful Dis/Connection: Bringing Digital (Inter)Dependent Relations Out From the Shadows of Autonomy
toc.abstractEn: A conceptual analysis argues that digital disconnection should be understood through interdependence and care rather than an ideal of autonomous withdrawal from devices and platforms.

toc.title: Do Experts Agree About Misinformation? Evidence From Three Annual Surveys
toc.abstractEn: Three annual expert surveys assess agreement about the prevalence, spread, and effects of misinformation, identifying both areas of consensus and persistent uncertainty.

toc.title: Exploring the Predictors and Outcomes of Perceived Algorithm Responsiveness in Social Media Feeds: Combining Longitudinal and Computational Methods
toc.abstractEn: Longitudinal and computational analyses examine which message cues predict perceived algorithm responsiveness and how those perceptions relate to later social-media use.

toc.title: Women Sustaining TikTok as Supplementary Information Infrastructure for Flexible Work Arrangements: Gendered Conditions, Community and Surveillance
toc.abstractEn: The study examines how women use TikTok as an informal information infrastructure for interpreting flexible work, while navigating gendered community support and surveillance.

toc.title: “I Share Your Sentiment”—A Longitudinal Study of Facebook Post Sentiment and Sharing
toc.abstractEn: A population-level analysis of Norwegian political parties’ Facebook posts from 2016 to 2025 tests how negative, positive, and neutral sentiment predicts sharing over time.

toc.title: Fandom Rupture in the Movement Society: Reactive Collective Participation Through Affective Practices
toc.abstractEn: The article explains how affective practices sustain movement-like participation after an external shock draws heterogeneous fandom actors into a shared platform arena before a collective goal has formed.
